subject: Score: paper
value: North America: 9 x 12 inches or more, 11 x 17 inches or less. Europe: B4 JIS (257 x 364 mm) or A3 (297 x 420 mm). Portrait format.

subject: Score: staff
value: The smallest staff that a conductor can read is 4 mm. One orchestra asks for 4 to 5 mm.

subject: Score: margins
value: Top and bottom 20 to 23 mm, left and right 17 to 20 mm.

subject: Score: order
value: Woodwinds, brass, timpani and percussion and harp and keyboards, voices, strings. In each group from high to low.

subject: Score: bar lines
value: The bar lines are continuous in each family of instruments.

subject: Score: names
value: Full names at the first system, abbreviations after it. A staff for more than one player says how many players it has.

subject: Score: tempo
value: Above the highest staff and above the first violins on each page.

subject: Score: bar numbers
rule: Place and size of the bar numbers
value: At the start of each system (not the first), above the clef of the highest staff, 10 to 13 point, italic. A different way: each bar, below the system.

subject: Score: rehearsal marks
rule: Place and size of the rehearsal marks
value: At landmarks of the music. Above the highest staff of the woodwinds and of the strings; for a large orchestra above more families. Bold, in a box, 19 to 23 point. A reader finds a mark with not more than one page turn.

subject: Score: page numbers
value: Right pages have odd numbers in the upper right corner, left pages have even numbers in the upper left corner. 14 to 16 point. Page 1 is the first page of music.

subject: Score: first page
value: Title, composer, copyright, and all instruments (also those that do not play at the start). "Transposed score" or "Score in C" in the upper left corner.

subject: Score: cover
value: Title and composer are prominent. The title is as in a concert programme. The name and address of the publisher, and a date of the print or of the revision.

subject: Score: front pages
value: The full instrumentation: doublings, the keys of the transposing instruments, each percussion instrument (with the ranges that are necessary), and the number of percussion players. The durations. Special instructions, a diagram of the stage for an unusual plan, an explanation of unusual notation. A programme note.

subject: Score: transposition
rule: Transposed score or score in C
value: One orchestra asks for a transposed score. The score must say which type it is.

subject: Score: empty staves
rule: Staves of players who do not play
value: Do not hide empty staves if the reduction is not large. Keep the full score where possible.

subject: Score: shared staves
value: Two players of one instrument share a staff where possible (for example flutes 1 and 2). One publisher made a score of 41 possible staves with 22 staves.

subject: Score: percussion
value: From high to low by pitch, or by player. The same plan for all of the work.

subject: Paper
value: 100 to 120 g/m2, white or off-white, not shiny. Music on the two sides of each sheet. The parts lie flat on the stand.

subject: Parts: paper
value: 9 x 12 inches or more, 11 x 14 inches or less; A4 is the smallest size, B4 is the most common. Sizes of many publishers: 9 x 12, 9.5 x 12.5, 10 x 13 inches. A digital part: not larger than 9 x 12 inches.

subject: Parts: staff
value: 7.5 mm is the best. 7.0 mm is possible for winds. Less than 7.0 mm is not acceptable, more than 8.5 mm is not good.

subject: Parts: margins
value: 20 mm (0.75 inch) around the music.

subject: Parts: systems
value: 8 to 10 for an instrument with many ledger lines (flute, violin, tuba). Not more than 12.

subject: Parts: page turns
value: The player has the time to turn the page: think of the tempo and of the instrument. A rest of many bars is at the end of a page, if possible.

subject: Parts: clefs
value: At the start of each line. A warning at the end of the line before a change.

subject: Parts: bar numbers
value: At the start of each line, not in each bar. A rest of many bars can show its range of bar numbers.

subject: Parts: cues
value: After a long rest, a cue from an instrument that the player can hear, in the key of the part. Tempo and metre changes show also in rests.

subject: Parts: doubling
value: A clear instruction when to change, and the name of the instrument at the subsequent entry.

subject: Parts: headers
value: The front of a part has the title, the composer, and the instrument (with its key). Each subsequent page has the name of the instrument, the title, and the page number.

subject: Parts: one player
rule: One part for each wind player
value: Flute 1 and flute 2 are separate parts. Each string section has one part. A division that is complex has separate staves.

subject: Parts: percussion
value: A key of the notation at the start of a percussion part that is complex. The timpani have a separate part.

subject: Parts: harp and strings
value: The pedal changes of the harp are not printed. Bowings are printed only for a special effect.

subject: Files
value: "COMPOSER work title 00 - score.pdf", "COMPOSER work title 01 - flute 1.pdf", and so on, in the sequence of the score.
